what_it_does: This paper optimizes linear solvers (mathematical routines that solve systems of equations) for Intel GPUs when the matrix structure is irregular. Traditional matrix operations assume dense, uniform data layouts, but many real scientific problems have variable-sized blocks and indirect memory access patterns. These irregular patterns waste GPU processing resources. This work applies ESIMD (Explicit SIMD, a GPU programming model) to efficiently handle variable block sizes and indirect access patterns while keeping the GPU's 512-bit vector registers well-utilized.
method_in_detail: The optimization uses ESIMD vectorization techniques customized for block-sparse structures with variable row lengths. The implementation achieves performance within 10 percent of the theoretical peak bandwidth available on the GPU.
